details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:187-225, 747-754 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The cap clock DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_CLOCK_START_EPOCH starts before the pre-dispatch lookup at line 748, but the cap is checked only inside the rate-limit branch of dispatch_workflow(). So when the lookup spends up to 30+60+120 s backing off and then succeeds, and the dispatch also succeeds, the full completion watch starts without any cap check.
  WHY: For validation-refresh, 4 + 210 + 5520 = 5734 s goes past the 5700 s step timeout, so the runner can kill the step before the watcher's timeout-cancel handling (#9532) runs. All three reviewers rated it MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash say this path already exists on the merge base and was not made longer by this PR.
- changelog.d/10197-dispatch-rate-limit-wait.md:15 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The operator sentence "a secondary limit (60 s) is now absorbed in every gate dispatch step" is false when the pre-dispatch lookup was itself rate-limited. In that case rl_spent is already about 210 s, and 210 + 60 is over the caps of validation-refresh (110), standalone validate (180), internal-memory-maintenance (230) and orchestrate (240).
  WHY: In the rate-limited-PAT case, four of the five gate steps fail at once with outcome=cap_reached instead of absorbing the wait. The script works as designed; this is a documentation defect. All three reviewers rated it NIT.
- changelog.d/10197-dispatch-rate-limit-wait.md:6 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The claim that the cap keeps "a step... inside its timeout-minutes and its timeout cancel still runs" holds only when the dispatch itself is rate-limited. On the success path, where the lookup backs off and then succeeds, no cap check runs. The budget test (tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:383-412) also leaves the lookup backoff out of its formula.
  WHY: For validation-refresh, the worst case of about 5904 s exceeds the 5700 s timeout, so the step can be killed with no timeout-cancel diagnostics, which contradicts the new documentation. The overrun itself is inherited from the base.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:198-216 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When the cap is reached, the script returns 1 without trying the remaining retries but still logs "failed after N attempts".
  WHY: The message can mislead operators about how many attempts were actually made, for example 1 attempt when DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 5.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Replaying the evidence (403 rate limit at 03:14:38, reset at 03:23:03) ends in a successful dispatch after one wait of about 8.5 minutes."
  expected_change_site: the "Dispatch & watch — update_workflows (allow_workflow_edits=false)" step in .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "410", near lines 4037-4039) and dispatch_workflow() in scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh (cap check at line 212)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The step caps the wait at 410 s but the replay needs about 505-510 s, so the cap check at line 212 rejects the wait (0 + 510 > 410) and the step fails with outcome=cap_reached. With a rate-limited lookup it also fails, since 210 + about 300 > 410. The changelog (changelog.d/10197-dispatch-rate-limit-wait.md line 15) says the incident step "still fails that step". Only test_primary_rate_limit_replay_waits_for_reset_then_dispatches shows success, and only under the default 1500 s cap. The issue also says to lower caps rather than raise timeout-minutes, so this needs a plan-level choice. Severity ratings: gemini, minimax and luna BLOCKER; sonnet and glm MAJOR.
- requirement: "The full test suite passes."
  expected_change_site: full-suite verification for the PR head SHA
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The pre-push gate is status=unverified, with 55 inherited failures and unverified timeouts (tests/test_orchestrate_poll_promote_cycle.py baseline_timeout, tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py timeout). No passing full-suite run is recorded. The failing files are outside the PR's changed files. Severity ratings: gemini, minimax and luna MAJOR; glm NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly skipped this as an inherited failure the PR cannot close.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- changelog.d/10197-dispatch-rate-limit-wait.md:line 15, "a secondary limit (60 s) is now absorbed in every gate dispatch step" | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sentence is not always true. The cap clock starts before the pre-dispatch lookup (scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh line 748), and that lookup can spend 30+60+120 s (comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh lines 134-147). After that, rl_spent is about 210 (dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh lines 207-212), and 210 + 60 is over the caps of validation-refresh 110, standalone validate 180, internal-memory-maintenance 230 and orchestrate 240.
  WHY: Those steps end at once with outcome=cap_reached instead of absorbing the wait. The README row and agents fragment are correct. Fix: qualify the sentence ("when the pre-dispatch run lookup itself was not rate-limited").
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Replaying the evidence (403 rate limit at 03:14:38, reset at 03:23:03) ends in a successful dispatch after one wait of about 8.5 minutes." (AC1, together with the Goal)
  Expected change site: the "Dispatch & watch — update_workflows (allow_workflow_edits=false)" step in .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (env block added near line 4037, DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "410") and dispatch_workflow() in scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh (cap check at line 212)
  Evidence of absence: The replay needs about 510 s, so line 212 refuses it (0 + 510 > 410). With a rate-limited lookup, 210 + about 300 > 410. Only the script-level test with the default cap of 1500 succeeds, and the changelog confirms the incident step still fails. Fixing it needs a plan-level choice; the editor deferred it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- NOTE: The pass-1 MAJOR finding at scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh lines 187-190 was judged real but pre-existing (the RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF loop at comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh lines 134-147), so it was not reported as a regression. COMPLETION_DEADLINE (line 848) was confirmed to start from DISPATCH_STARTED_AT. AC3 was skipped as an inherited failure.
- HARDENING: tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py, last assert of test_pre_lookup_failure_then_wait_restarts_the_fallback_window ("window_start >= int(time.time()) + 210 + int(waits[0].group(2)) - 30"). It mixes the STUB_CLOCK_BASE fake clock with time.time() read after the subprocess exits, so it fails if the run takes more than about 29 s. Fix: return STUB_CLOCK_BASE from _run and assert window_start >= base + 210 + wait - 1 (4 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:198-216 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cap for rate-limit waits is checked only inside the dispatch_workflow loop, after a failed dispatch attempt.
  WHY: DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_CLOCK_START_EPOCH is set at line 748, before the gh_api_safe lookup. Lookup retry time is not held within DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS, so the job can exceed its step timeout.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:748-754 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cap clock starts at the beginning of the script, but the pre-dispatch run-id lookup (line 753) is not gated by the cap.
  WHY: Lookup retries can use up a large part of the step timeout, and the runner can kill the step before the watcher's failure handling runs.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:198-216 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: On reaching the cap, the script returns 1 without the remaining retries but logs "failed after N attempts".
  WHY: The message misstates how many attempts were actually made, for example 1 attempt when DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 5.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Replaying the evidence (403 rate limit at 03:14:38, reset at 03:23:03) ends in a successful dispatch after one wait of about 8.5 minutes."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, the `Dispatch & watch — update_workflows` step, and `dispatch_workflow()` in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh`
  Evidence of absence: The cap is 410 s but the incident needs about 510 s, so the cap check rejects the wait. The changelog says this wait will still fail.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The full test suite passes."
  Expected change site: Full-suite verification for the PR.
  Evidence of absence: The pre-push gate is unverified, with 55 inherited failures and one unverified timeout. No passing full-suite run is provided.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- HARDENING: tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py, test_pre_lookup_failure_then_wait_restarts_the_fallback_window. int(time.time()) can drift from STUB_CLOCK_BASE on a slow run. Fix: pass STUB_CLOCK_BASE back from _run and use it in the assertion (4 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:dispatch_workflow(), cap check only inside rate-limit branch at lines 198-225; clock start at line ~747 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cap clock starts before the pre-dispatch lookup, but the cap is enforced only on a rate-limited dispatch failure. After the 30+60+120 s backoff in gh_api_safe_quiet_print, a dispatch that succeeds first time goes into the completion watch with no cap check.
  WHY: For validation-refresh (cap 110, watch 5520 s, timeout 5700 s), 4 + 210 + 5520 = 5734 s goes 34 s over budget. The runner can SIGTERM the step before the #9532 timeout-cancel runs. The changelog's claim that the step stays inside timeout-minutes holds only on the rate-limit branch.
- changelog.d/10197-dispatch-rate-limit-wait.md:line 15 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: With a rate-limited PAT, the lookup backoff (scripts/comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh lines 134-147) makes rl_spent >= 210 s. Then validation-refresh 110, standalone validate 180, internal-memory-maintenance 230 and orchestrate 240 trip the cap on the first dispatch wait; only update_workflows (410) absorbs it.
  WHY: Operators expect every gate step to absorb a secondary limit; in fact four of five fail at once with cap_reached. The README row and agents fragment are correct.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Replaying the evidence (403 rate limit at 03:14:38, reset at 03:23:03) ends in a successful dispatch after one wait of about 8.5 minutes."
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, the Dispatch & watch — update_workflows step (DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS="410"), and dispatch_workflow() in scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh
